PLAN:
1. VERIFY — confirm call-site count before editing:
   - grep `gate_decision(` in daily_part_06.py → expect exactly 3 sites (two `_cell`/`_leaf_cell` variants plus any third).
   - grep `gate_decision(` in hourly_engine.py → expect exactly 1 site (the `_axis_vals` block in live_signal).
   - At hourly site, verify which stamped variables are in local scope: `cross_model_std` from `_wx`, `ou_z`, `cloud_div_pct`, `wind_*`, `dewpoint_spread_f`, `mins_to_formation` (`min_to_settle` on `o`), `settle_hour`, `p_formed`. `model_run_age_h` confirmed absent → stays None.
   - At each daily site, verify the cell/evidence dict carries: `mins_to_formation`, `model_run_age_h`, `cross_model_std`, `settle_hour`, `p_formed`, `ou_*`, weather axes — and whether they live on `_cell`, on the stamped evidence row, or both. Use whichever object is authoritative at that exact line.
   - Confirm AXIS_BUCKETERS key list (10 axes) from adaptive_tree.py — the helper keys must match exactly, character for character.

2. ADD `build_axis_values(**kwargs)` in learning.py:
   - Signature: `def build_axis_values(**kwargs) -> dict:` returning `{k: kwargs.get(k) for k in _CANONICAL_AXES}` where `_CANONICAL_AXES` is a literal tuple copied from (or imported as) `list(AXIS_BUCKETERS.keys())` — import from adaptive_tree to avoid drift: `from adaptive_tree import AXIS_BUCKETERS` then `tuple(AXIS_BUCKETERS.keys())`.
   - Pure function: no side effects, no defaults beyond None, no clamping, no bucketing (bucketers already handle None → fail-closed).
   - Import-cycle check: learning.py must not import adaptive_tree at module top if adaptive_tree imports learning.py. If a cycle exists, define the axis tuple locally in learning.py with a comment tying it to AXIS_BUCKETERS, and add a one-line test/assert at module load of adaptive_tree comparing key sets.

3. HOURLY WIRING (hourly_engine.py, 1 site):
   - Replace the hardcoded `_axis_vals` dict with `_axis_vals = build_axis_values(mins_to_formation=o.get('min_to_settle'), settle_hour=o.get('settle_hour'), ou_z=o.get('ou_z'), cross_model_std=<the _wx-derived value already in scope>, cloud_div_pct=..., wind_speed_mph=..., wind_gust_mph=..., dewpoint_spread_f=..., p_formed=..., model_run_age_h=None)` using exactly the same sources used in the stamping block above it.
   - Do NOT fabricate model_run_age_h — pass None.
   - Reuse the same dict for evidence stamping where keys overlap (single construction, two consumers) — only if the stamping block and gate call are in the same function scope; otherwise construct at each point from the same underlying locals.

4. DAILY WIRING (daily_part_06.py, 3 sites):
   - At each `gate_decision(_cell)` / `gate_decision(_leaf_cell)` call, build `_axis_vals = build_axis_values(...)` from the values already on the cell/evidence (per Fact 1: `mins_to_formation`, `model_run_age_h` from ensemble run_time, `cross_model_std`, `settle_hour`, `p_formed`, `ou_*` are stamped upstream).
   - Pass as `axis_values=_axis_vals` at all 3 sites.
   - If the three sites share a helper (e.g., a common `_evaluate_cell` path), construct once there; do not duplicate construction logic in three places if one choke point exists.

5. COVERAGE WARNING (optional, in recompute_tree):
   - Track set of axis keys observed non-None across recent gate calls (module-level counter or log-line). In recompute_tree, if a node's `split_axis` was never observed (or >50% None) since last recompute, emit `logger.warning("axis %s unreachable: absent from gate calls", axis)`.
   - Logging only — no gating, no promotion changes.

6. TESTS:
   - Unit: build_axis_values with all keys → full dict; with subset → missing keys present as None; with extra kwargs → ignored.
   - Unit: gate_decision with full axis dict on a tree-licensed path now resolves to a tree node (previously flat); gate_decision with all-None dict still returns flat (fail-closed regression guard).
   - Integration smoke: run one daily cell through each of the 3 patched sites and assert resolve_license receives non-None axis_values (spy/log assertion).
   - Regression: run existing test suite; confirm zero behavior change when axis_values omitted.

RISKS:
- Import cycle learning.py ↔ adaptive_tree.py if helper imports AXIS_BUCKETERS (mitigation: local tuple + assertion, per step 2).
- Variable-name mismatch at hourly site: stamped evidence keys may differ from local variable names (`min_to_settle` vs `mins_to_formation` already observed) — copying names blindly will reintroduce silent None.
- One of the 3 daily sites may execute before stamping (values not yet on the cell) → helper yields all-None → still flat, silently. Must confirm ordering at each site.
- p_formed may not exist at the hourly gate call point (Fact 3 lists it as omitted; Fact 1 does not list hourly stamping of p_formed) — verify before including; pass None if genuinely absent rather than inventing it.
- Helper returning dict-with-None-keys vs callers omitting keys: bucketer behavior must treat both identically (it does, per Fact 4 — but confirm bucketers use `.get`).
- Commit straight to main: no staged rollout; a wiring bug that maps a wrong value (e.g., gust vs sustained wind swapped) changes licensing paths silently. Exact-name verification at each site is the only mitigation.

CHECKPOINTS:
- [ ] grep confirms exactly 1 hourly site, 3 daily sites, no other gate_decision callers anywhere in repo.
- [ ] AXIS_BUCKETERS key list pasted into review and matched against helper output keys (automated assert).
- [ ] At each of 4 sites: table of axis → source variable/field verified from the code at that line (not inferred).
- [ ] Daily sites confirmed to execute after evidence stamping.
- [ ] Import graph: no new cycle introduced.
- [ ] Fail-closed regression test: all-None axis dict → flat gate, same result as pre-change.
- [ ] Reachability test: at least one known tree-licensed path resolves via tree after the change.
- [ ] Coverage warning emits when expected; does not raise.
- [ ] Full test suite green; diff touches only learning.py (helper), adaptive_tree.py (warning), hourly_engine.py (1 site), daily_part_06.py (3 sites) + tests.

IF_FAIL:
- Symptom: decisions still flat after wiring → instrument resolve_license to log received axis dict + bucketer output per axis at one licensed node; identify which key is None/misnamed; fix mapping only. Do not change gate logic.
- Symptom: import cycle at startup → fall back to local axis tuple in learning.py (step 2 alternative).
- Symptom: any test shows different sizing/promotion/licensing outcome for previously working paths → revert entire commit (single commit, straight revert on main) and re-audit value mappings; never patch gate behavior to compensate.
- Symptom: daily values absent at call time (stamping-after-call ordering) → move the gate call or the stamping, whichever preserves existing semantics; if ambiguous, leave that site flat and file follow-up rather than reordering logic blindly.
- Symptom: wrong-value mapping discovered post-merge (e.g., licensing on gust where split trained on sustained) → revert immediately; fail-closed default means revert is always safe.

DECISION_RULES:
- Rule: only keys in AXIS_BUCKETERS may appear in build_axis_values output; no caller-specific extras.
- Rule: any axis whose value does not exist at a call site is passed as None — never estimated, backfilled, or defaulted. Applies specifically to hourly model_run_age_h and hourly p_formed unless verification proves presence.
- Rule: if any daily site turns out to run before stamping, that site stays un-wired in this commit rather than reordering code.
- Rule: helper construction may be shared between stamping and gate call only within one function scope; no cross-function threading of the dict through signatures beyond the existing axis_values parameter.
- Rule: zero tolerance for behavior drift in the None path — if any regression test differs pre/post change with axis_values absent, the change is wrong by definition; revert.
- Rule: coverage warning is log-only; it must never raise, gate, or alter recompute output.
- Rule: single atomic commit to main; if any checkpoint fails, fix forward or revert the whole commit — no partial fixes stacked on top.
